label: Eventing visual/online debugger
type: a live, real-time JavaScript debugger for a Function's handler code, integrating with the Chrome DevTools protocol, enabled per-Function or Service-wide via the `enable_debugger` setting. NOT Server-only despite server/8.0/eventing-debugging-and-diagnosability.md being the only full page on it - Capella's own eventing-Terminologies.md 'Debug' glossary entry describes the identical mechanism, just as one glossary entry rather than a dedicated page.
evidence: Couchbase Server, for its Eventing Service framework, includes a powerful full function online real-time JavaScript Debugger. Debug is a special flag on a Function. The Debug option integrates seamlessly with the Google Chrome Web Browser.
The default Eventing debug port is 9140.
Enables the Eventing service debugger. This setting is available globally or at the function scope level.
note: CORRECTS THIS ROUND'S OWN FRAMING. The dispatch briefing treated eventing-debugging-and-diagnosability.md as one of two pages with 'no Capella twin' and reasoned from that toward a memory-management asymmetry (see docs-issues/server-eventing-memory-quota-premise-contradicted). The debugger itself is not the asymmetry - what's genuinely Server-only on that page is the node/OS-administration content (static_config editing, NAT workaround, log paths, cbcollect_info). A 'no twin' page can be no-twin for content reasons unrelated to the feature it's about.
relates_to_competency_question: Can a Function's handler code be debugged live, step by step, and is that a Server-only capability?
